title: runtime: add tracing spans + exemplars for KV compaction/eviction
author: Julian Moore
description: This PR adds distributed tracing around KV cache compaction and eviction so we can correlate allocator/scheduler behavior with p95/p99 latency spikes during bursty mixed-length decode workloads. Motivation: we already export counters for fragmentation/bytes-moved, but during canaries and support escalations it has been hard to answer “did compaction/eviction happen on the critical path for *this* request?” This change introduces low-overhead, budget-aware spans emitted only when compaction/eviction work is actually performed, plus trace exemplars that tie key allocator events to existing latency histograms. Scope: (1) new spans for compaction steps and eviction decisions, (2) consistent semantic attributes (bytes moved, pages relocated, fragmentation ratio before/after, budget source), (3) exemplar emission on tail-latency buckets when compaction/eviction coincides with elevated decode latency, and (4) guardrails to avoid regressions (sampling, thresholds, and a runtime flag). No allocator behavior is changed; this is observability-only. Rollout: behind runtime config `kv_compaction.tracing_enabled` (default off) and `kv_compaction.tracing_sample_rate` (default 0.01) for internal canary first; SRE can override per-pool. Notes: This PR is intended to land after the fragmentation counters PR (pr-19342) but does not strictly depend on it; attributes will be populated opportunistically when metrics are available.
implementation_notes: Span model: We emit a parent span `runtime.kv.compaction` for each compaction run (one per scheduler iteration when work is done), and a child span `runtime.kv.compaction.relocate` per relocation batch. Evictions emit `runtime.kv.eviction` spans with decision attributes. All spans are attached to the request trace context when the scheduler is operating on a request-backed iteration; background compaction (if enabled later) will create its own root span with `kv.compaction.mode=background`. Exemplar model: when a request sees decode latency above the configured threshold and `compaction_bytes_moved>0` or `evictions>0` occurred in the same scheduling window, we attach an exemplar linking the latency histogram bucket to the current trace/span ID. Attributes (stable names): `kv.compaction.bytes_moved`, `kv.compaction.pages_moved`, `kv.compaction.duration_ms`, `kv.compaction.fragmentation_before`, `kv.compaction.fragmentation_after`, `kv.compaction.budget_ms`, `kv.compaction.budget_bytes`, `kv.compaction.budget_source` (scheduler|background), `kv.eviction.count`, `kv.eviction.reason` (oom_avoidance|fragmentation|tier_pressure), `kv.eviction.tier`, `kv.eviction.pinned_skipped`, `scheduler.phase` (prefill|decode|boundary). Performance guardrails: spans are created only if (a) tracing enabled, (b) sample gate passes, and (c) work done > 0. Attribute population avoids string formatting on hot path; we use integer/double attributes only. Exemplar emission is separately gated via `kv_compaction.exemplars_enabled` (default off) to avoid cardinality surprises until dashboards are in place.

ci_summary: Builds: linux-gpu-runtime (pass), runtime-unit (pass), runtime-integration (pass), lint (pass). Perf: perf-smoke (initial fail due to tracing enabled in one test env; fixed by ensuring defaults off + adding explicit opt-in test), perf-canary-sim (pass).
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we standardize attribute names to align with the metrics standard doc? Please avoid ad-hoc `compactionBytesMoved` style and use `kv.compaction.bytes_moved` etc. Also: confirm exemplars won’t explode cardinality in dashboards.

Julian Moore (author): Updated to a dedicated semconv header with snake_case dotted names and added `exemplars_enabled` flag default OFF. Exemplar emission uses trace_id only (no request IDs) and is gated on tail-latency threshold + sample gate.

Samir Qureshi: Concern about span creation on the hot decode loop. Can we guarantee we don’t allocate when no work is done? Also please include fragmentation before/after so we can validate effectiveness.

Julian Moore (author): Span builder is invoked only when `bytes_moved > 0 || evictions > 0`. Fragmentation before/after populated from allocator snapshot already taken for metrics; if not available, we omit the attribute (not set) rather than compute.

Caleb Johnson: For exemplar linkage, please use the telemetry platform’s histogram API that supports exemplars; don’t DIY attach trace IDs to labels. Also ensure we propagate trace context through scheduler boundaries correctly (prefill/decode).

Julian Moore (author): Switched to `Histogram::RecordWithExemplar()` path; no labels added. Added scheduler hook to carry current span context across the boundary step and a unit test that verifies spans nest under the request root span.

Sean Gallagher: SRE ask: add a short doc snippet listing flags and a runbook-y section: what to look for in traces, and what attributes indicate compaction is on critical path. Also, can we add a safeguard so we don’t emit spans for tiny moves (<1 page)?
Julian Moore (author): Added internal doc + example trace screenshots (text description) and minimum threshold `kv_compaction.tracing_min_bytes` default 262144 (256KiB).
Omar El-Sayed: Looks good. Please add a regression test ensuring eviction span includes tier + reason. Also clarify that eviction span is emitted per decision batch, not per sequence, to avoid spam.
Julian Moore (author): Added unit test for required attributes and ensured eviction span is per batch (one span per scheduler iteration, with `kv.eviction.count`).
testing: Unit: `runtime_telemetry_test` (span attributes + context propagation), `kv_eviction_policy_test` (span attribute presence), `scheduler_trace_context_test` (parent/child relationships). Manual: ran `bench_frag_churn --mixed-length --burst` on A100 staging with tracing enabled at 1% sample; verified traces show `runtime.kv.compaction` spans aligning with latency spikes and that no spans are emitted when compaction disabled or when no bytes moved.
rollout_plan: Land behind flags (defaults off). Enable in internal perf canary at 0.5–1% sample for 24h. If span volume or overhead is higher than expected, lower sample rate or disable exemplars first. After internal validation, SRE can enable per hosted canary pool during runtime-1.22 rollout for incident correlation only.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into `main` after perf-smoke fix and approvals from runtime + observability + SRE.
linked_incidents_or_support: None directly; intended to support investigation/rollback criteria during compaction canary and future tail-latency escalations.
